what_this_is: Every source the melanoma assessment draws on, rebuilt on 2026-08-29 from the page's own sources section rather than from a sweep of its links. The previous version was built by sweeping links, which collected the webfont CDN and the stylesheet host as S001, S002 and S003 -- typed 'press', with empty used_for fields and no titles at all. That bug was found and documented while building issue two's source list, and was never fixed here. It surfaced again when the source ledger reported this page completely clean: with no titles, the audit could not match a single sentence to a single source, and an audit that matches nothing is indistinguishable from an audit that finds nothing.

sources.title: Weber JS, Khattak MA, Carlino MS, et al. Individualized neoantigen therapy mRNA-4157 (V940) plus pembrolizumab in resected melanoma: 3-year update from the mRNA-4157-P201 (KEYNOTE-942) trial. ASCO 2024, abstract LBA9512
sources.used_for: The three-year readout this page describes as the point at which the recurrence interval cleared the no-effect line: HR 0.510, 95% CI 0.288-0.906. All three figures are in this deck.

access.by: Fred Ugast, who supplied the presentation PDF on 2026-09-01
access.note:
THIS ENTRY EXISTS BECAUSE THE PAGE ALREADY DEPENDED ON IT AND THE LEDGER DID NOT KNOW. The page names 'the three-year readout at ASCO 2024' and attributes HR 0.510 (0.288-0.906) to it, and S007's own note says the three-year figures 'are taken from the ASCO 2024 presentation of the same analysis'. There was no source row for it. B9 did not catch this one because the page names the presentation without linking it, so a check that reads anchors could not see it -- a limit of B9 worth recording beside the case it did catch.

It also re-confirms, independently, that 0.510 is the figure the evidence carries to three decimals. The 0.51 that a precision check flagged on 2026-09-01 is only ever the company press release.

A WebFetch of the same URL DID return the page and confirmed the sentence this page quotes, verbatim: "Notably, patients with resected stage IIB or IIC melanoma can face risks of recurrence and melanoma-specific mortality similar to those observed in stage III disease."

THE STATE IS NOT CHANGED ON THAT EVIDENCE. sources.title: Eggermont AMM, Chiarion-Sileni V, Grob J-J, et al. Prolonged Survival in Stage III Melanoma with Ipilimumab Adjuvant Therapy. N Engl J Med 2016;375:1845-1855 (EORTC 18071)
sources.used_for: The one adjuvant checkpoint inhibitor that has reported a statistically significant overall survival benefit against placebo as a prespecified endpoint. It is a CTLA-4 inhibitor, not a PD-1 inhibitor, which is why the page's claim about PD-1 inhibitors survives and why the sentence now says so.

access.note:
Entered 2026-09-01 because the counterexample hunt narrowed a universal negative on this page and named this paper as what breaks it. A finding is not a source: the sentence citing it does not stand until these bytes are held.

2026-09-01: acquire_sources fetched the PubMed page and REFUSED it -- 0 of 12 title words, no DOI/PMID/NCT in the bytes, so whatever came back was not the record. WebFetch returned the page's metadata (title, journal, PMID, DOI) but not the abstract. Nothing here licenses a claim about what this trial found.

The page does not make one. The sentence the counterexample hunt narrowed now says what the claim is NOT about -- PD-1 inhibitors, not checkpoint inhibitors as a class -- rather than asserting the ipilimumab result from a finding. Writing a page correction out of a gate finding instead of a document is the error this repository recorded three times today.

2026-09-01, and this is the part worth keeping: the errata check looked S012 up by its PMID and found that IT CARRIES A FORMAL CORRECTION (erratum, PMID 31442371) which nobody here has read. Had the sentence gone in from the counterexample hunt's finding, the page would have cited, as the fact that broke a pattern, a paper we do not hold and whose correction we have not seen.

sources._to_do: Get the NEJM paper or its PMC copy and add it, then the sentence can name what broke the broader pattern instead of stepping around it.
sources._not_cited_on_the_page: This source is recorded, not used. The page makes no claim about EORTC 18071; the sentence the hunt narrowed says only what it is NOT about. The entry exists so the next person knows why, and so that acquiring the paper is a task rather than a rediscovery.

also_called_note: The role-nouns the page uses for a source. These must identify the DOCUMENT, not its subject: 'KEYNOTE-942' is a trial that three of these sources report on, and listing it as an alias for all three made every sentence about the trial match all three at once -- so the one source marked `blocked` absorbed the blame for claims the read sources actually support. The ledger audit matches sentences to sources by these plus the title's trial and journal names; a reference the page makes that is not listed here is invisible to the audit.
